choices.A: Construct the midpoint of \(AB\) and draw a perpendicular to \(l\) through the midpoint. Its foot is \(P\).
choices.B: Draw a perpendicular to \(l\) through \(A\). Its foot is \(P\).
choices.C: Construct the perpendicular bisector of \(AB\). Its intersection with \(l\) is \(P\).
choices.D: Construct \(A'\), the reflection of \(A\) across \(l\), and draw \(A'B\). Its intersection with \(l\) is \(P\).

question: \(A\) and \(B\) lie on the same side of line \(l\). How can a point \(P\) be found on \(l\) to minimize \(PA+PB\)?
solution: \(PA=PA'\), so \(PA+PB=PA'+PB\), which is minimized when \(A'\), \(P\), and \(B\) are collinear.
